summary: Nora can now say which rooms her group has on each network, whether each network is connected, and how busy each room is, and she can read what is being said in the group's room on another network.
details: Two new tools. room_list lists the rooms of the group she is being asked from: the network, the room's name, whether that network is up, reconnecting or waiting for a person, how many members it has, how many messages arrived in the last 24 hours and when someone last spoke. room_read returns the recent messages of one of those rooms, taken by the name room_list gives or by its network.

Other groups stay private. In any room she says only that she is in other groups as well, never which ones and never how many. Asking room_read for another group's room gets the same answer as asking for a room that does not exist.
No room id and no member name leaves either tool. A room with no name in the room table is called by its network.
What room_read returns is marked as chat other people wrote, never an instruction to her, the same way her own conversation's history already is.
Both tools read the same room table and connection checks as the where-you-are block she already gets every turn, so the two cannot disagree about which rooms exist.
limitations: A room's member count and its messages are read from the room's primary id in the room table. Messages that arrived under an older id form listed in also_ids are not counted or returned.
Routing for the two tools has test cases in the tool-selection suite but has not been measured against a live model yet.
